page.layout: One page of text in a single column; no margin notes, no running head beyond the printed header line at the top, and no text below the column except the catchword-free last line "Hispanias" set at the right, which is part of the running text. Printed header at top: "Cap.70." at left, "AVGVSTINVS" at right.

main_text.p: cata vero est hæc Priscillianistarum hæresis, non à Priscilla quidem, quæ fuit Montani scortum, & longè ante huius erroris principia vixit, etsi è Galatia, vbi plurimum Montaniste viguerunt, ortum protectumque hoc malum sentit Hieronymus: sed à Priscilliano homine, vt omnes authores scribunt, imprimisque Isidorus, & ipse Hispanus, & Hispalensis Episcopus, Hispano. Hic ab Helpidio rhetore in fide institutus & edoctus est: Helpidius autem ipse à Marco quodam Monacho, qui Ægyptia Memphi profugus, propter Valentis edictum de revocandis ad suas curias & ad publica munera subunda, Monachis (vt apparet ex L. Quidam ignauię sectatores. C. De Decurionibus lib.10.) venit in Hispaniam: sed iam Gnosticorum, & Manichæorum labe & veneno plane tabidus & infectus, quemadmodum inter Monachos errores omne genus aluntur. Ita igitur fascinatus Priscillianus, errorem suum in Hispania sparsit, sub Gratiano imperatore, & Damaso episcopo Romano, circa annum à Christo passo 348. etsi Sigeberto tardius hoc malum propagatum videtur: sed propagationem non autem originem ipsam spectauit Sigebertus. Gratanter autem & auidè exceptus à plurimis in Hispania, imprimis ab Instantio, & Saluiano episcopis, à quibus Priscillianus ipse episcopus constitutus est in Laletanis populis (qui sunt citerioris Hispaniæ, vt Plinius lib. 3. cap. 3. scribit) Adygino tamen Cordubensi episcopo reclamante, & eum errorem grauiter oppugnante. Peruicit tamen hæc lues & obtinuit, ita vt non tantum Hispanias

page.notes: Page is a single column of running text. The last line "Hispanias" is printed at the right, set apart, and is the start of a continuation word; it is transcribed as printed. Possible doubtful readings: "Montaniste" (printed "Montanistæ"), "Adygino" (printed "Adygino"), "Hispalensis" and "Hispano" as printed. "Sigeberto" and "Sigebertus" are printed as such (the text is garbled in the scan at several places; the scan is faint in the lower lines, especially "Peruicit tamen" and "obtinuit"). Some words are blurred by show-through and are marked [?] where not certain: "Priscilla" near the top appears clearly as printed. Printed line "Hispanias" at the foot is the last printed word.
